header: DO NOT EDIT: regenerate with `python3 proofs/verus/gen_pin_tests.py <spec>`.
Each test mirrors one [pins] row of proofs/verus/uae_terminators_sync.txt and
drives the REAL transform (`unreachable_after_exit::transform`), not a copy of
it: the witness is built as `IrStmt`s and the assertions read the returned
`changed` flag, the surviving list length, and (where it matters) the nested
body length. The proof-side witness is named in each test's doc comment.

pins.note: Proof: trunc keeps the loop and drops the tail after it. Source: `while true; do tick; done; echo dead` loses the echo.
Proof: run past a loop whose body can break, and the tail prints. Source: a body `break` makes the loop escapable, so nothing is truncated.
Proof: a case-nested break still escapes the loop (bash's case captures nothing). Source: the tail survives.
Proof: an inner loop's break belongs to that loop, so the outer loop still never falls through. Source: the tail after the outer loop is dropped.
Proof: BreakCall (`break || exit 1`) escapes. Source: the control-call spelling makes the loop escapable and keeps the tail (the `parse-break-or` regression).
Proof: run stops at a break, so the following print never appears. Source: the same body truncates after the break even though the loop is escapable.

Proof: a continue ends its list like a break. Source: the nested list truncates after the continue, keeping the echo before it. The witness is a Block, not an infinite loop body: a break-free `while true` is itself a terminator, so the pass keeps it whole and never descends (the proof's `trunc` takes the same branch), which is a different fact from this pin.
Proof: an exit inside an if is not a terminator for the enclosing list. Source: an `if` may not take the arm, so the tail after it is kept and nothing changes.
Proof: a case-nested exit only aborts when the clause matches. Source: the case is not a terminator, so the tail survives.

Proof: a top-level return does not stop the list (bash errors and continues), but inside a function body it does. Source: the same split, which is the `in_fn` flag the pass threads; an `IrProgram` is the transform's input, so the top-level case is the pre-dispatch statement vector.
